newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-ENQVIST, BOETSCH MEET IN DAVIS CUP FINAL DRESS REHEARSAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST, BOETSCH MEET IN DAVIS CUP FINAL DRESS REHEARSAL.

text.p: Thomas Enqvist of Sweden and Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch face a Davis Cup final dress rehearsal when the meet in the semifinals of the Lyon Grand Prix on Saturday.

Enqvist, whose country host France in the Davis Cup final at the end of November, recovered from 5-3 down in the third set to beat Chilean Marcelo Rios 6-3 2-6 7-5 in the last quarter-final on Friday.
Boetsch made quick work of eliminating compatriot Lionel Roux 6-3 6-1.
Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov faces Tim Henman in the other semifinal, a repeat of their Wimbledon first round clash won by the Briton.
The number two seed beat Swede Magnus Gustafsson 5-7 7-5 6-3 while Henman beat Karol Kucera of Slovakia 7-6 6-2.
Number five seed Enqvist, said: "It will be an interesting match before the (Davis Cup) final. Boetsch is in good form at the moment. He is hitting the ball well and I don't expect it to be easy."

Enqvist showed resilience, recovering from a service break that put fourth seeded Rios in a commanding position and serving for the match at 5-3, to break back and reel off four games in a row for his victory.
Rios contributed to his downfall with a rather too relaxed attitude in that match-winning position -- as if he had already done enough -- and made a string of unforced errors.
He showed disgust at his performance by kicking his bag.
The result could jeopardise the chances of the Chilean world number 10 of qualifying for the year-end ATP championship, his main goal of the season.
French Open champion Kafelnikov, speaking about his clash with Gustafsson, said: "It was very tight throughout the match and Magnus really put me through a lot of work.
"He dictated play during the first two sets even though I managed to win the second. And in the third he always had me under pressure."
Kafelnikov will be pleased to know he can raise his game when it matters as he prepares to face Henman, who is looking to reach his first ATP Tour tournament final.
